prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, turning aryl amines into a routine, mechanism-guided disconnection
for the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: After the first round my configuration is unchanged: C-N coupling for Buchwald and Hartwig plus base editing for Liu. The round-1 exchange tested both parts and neither failed on facts. B039 has the cleanest mechanism and the sharpest attribution on the shortlist: two independent groups, a catalytic cycle that explains why bulky, electron-rich ligands made the reaction general, and two decades of use in medicinal and process chemistry. B062 is the part with the broadest explicit support (Aqvist, Chabes, Somfai and me) and every supporter agrees it is a chemically conceived capability that independent laboratories have reproduced. Two achievements within three names is still the arrangement that gives a defensible citation for each. I do not claim a unifying theme; I accept that the prize pairs a core molecule-making method with a chemical-biology tool and that the two citations must stand separately.
statement.case_against: I have not resolved the objection Aqvist and Chabes put to B039: the 2010 prize honoured Pd cross-coupling, and C-N coupling is a different bond and mechanism but may still read as an extension of that paradigm. The Kosugi and Migita-type chronology is recalled, not verified, and I would want the committee record to settle it before the citation is final. For B062, the method is about ten years old, clinical outcomes are still accumulating, Liu alone leaves Komor and Gaudelli out although Gaudelli's evolved TadA deaminase is real enzyme chemistry, and Kondo and Nishida's independent deaminase-fusion work (published within months of the first cytidine base editor, as I recall) is a genuine competing claim that a Liu-only citation does not remove. If the committee drops the second part, I would move to Liu, Komor and Gaudelli for base editing alone. A chair who supports a configuration that has only two explicit supporters should also say that his own view does not make a majority.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that B039 is an extension of a method honoured in 2010 and not a completely new capability, and calls this a difference of philosophy; he proposes B062 plus B066 (Liu; Crews and Handa) instead.
responses.response: I accept that this is a philosophy difference, but I would put it in concrete terms. The 2010 citation covers C-C bond formation; aryl amines were not accessible by that route, and the C-N work needed its own ligand classes and a different rate-limiting step, so it opened a new retrosynthetic disconnection rather than polishing an old one. That said, your configuration has a real advantage: it avoids the 2010 question entirely. My difficulty is B066 itself. The PROTAC concept and the cereblon glue mechanism are two stories joined by one citation, and with no bifunctional degrader approved I cannot yet say what was discovered, by whom and when without leaning on the clinic of the glue half. I am not moving on this, but I regard B062 plus B066 as the strongest rival configuration, and I thank you for pressing on Liu alone, which I now accept for the reasons you give.

responses.point: Chabes puts B062 alone first, prefers Liu alone in his file but Liu, Komor and Gaudelli in his opening and response text, and says he would reconsider only if the committee drops the second part.
responses.response: Your two laureate sets cannot both be the committee's, and I think we should settle this now. Komor and Gaudelli ran the decisive experiments, and Gaudelli's TadA evolution is chemistry in its own right, so I do not dismiss the trio. But Liu conceived and directed both editors, Kondo and Nishida would then be the obvious fourth and fifth names, and a prize that credits two trainees of one laboratory and excludes the independent group is harder to defend than Liu alone. I therefore keep Liu alone in a two-part prize and would support your trio only if B062 becomes the sole part. I am glad you accept that the clinical maturity question is open and does not weigh against you more than against me.

responses.point: Somfai shares my B039 plus B062 configuration, rejects adding Kosugi to the C-N credit, and asks that a nanopore-sequencing remark be corrected in the record.
responses.response: I agree that Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide reactions are a precursor and that the general catalytic systems belong to Buchwald and Hartwig, so I withdraw my worry about widening the credit and keep the two names. For the chair's record, since the chair's summary asked which ID is meant: my second alternative is B036 (biomolecular condensates), and my first is B066, as stated in my round-1 file. I did not rank nanopore sequencing second, and that candidate is not on this shortlist. On your remark that base editing is protein engineering as much as chemistry, I think the deaminase chemistry is the core, but I accept that Aili and you will weigh this differently.

responses.point: Aili ranks B066 as a molecular design principle, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and would accept Ciulli for Deshaies, while noting no bifunctional degrader is yet approved.
responses.response: Your argument that degradation is a transferable small-molecule design rule is the best case against my own configuration, and it has moved B066 up my list. I still think the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism are different findings, and your own uncertainty about whether to present them as one achievement or two is the point that blocks me. If the committee decides that the molecular-glue and PROTAC branches are one achievement and agrees on Crews, Handa and one of Deshaies or Ciulli, I would take B066 as a serious replacement for B039 as the partner of base editing, and I would not oppose it as the second part.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates first as a physical-chemical concept, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, and ranks C-N coupling sixth because of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: Your own caution about proximity and the contested in-cell evidence help me, because they are the same problems I raised: a physicist would like to see that the liquid description holds quantitatively for the condensates that matter, not only in vitro. I still find the thermodynamic picture of demixing attractive, and I keep B036 as an alternative. On Pd coupling, I note that you and Aqvist both rely on the 2010 overlap, so I take it as the main objection to B039 and I will say plainly that if the other members share it, I would prefer the committee to move B039 out than to narrow it.

uncertainties: Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize makes B039 read as an extension of a recognised paradigm, which Aqvist, Sparr and Chabes press and I do not fully rebut.
Dated priority for base editing: Komor and Gaudelli versus Nishida and Kondo, and Buchwald and Hartwig versus Kosugi and Migita-type precursors; my chronology is recalled, not verified.
Whether a two-part prize without a unifying theme will be accepted, or a single-achievement prize (B062 with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli) preferred.
Whether PROTACs and cereblon glues can be cited as one discovery, and whether a prize before approval of a bifunctional degrader is premature.
Whether the clinical record of base editing is mature enough by 2026.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has changed. My Lund connections (NanoLund, LTH, colleagues Somfai and Sparr) bear on none of the shortlisted candidates, and none of the credited names is known to me as a Lund colleague. I disclose again that I am a physicist chairing a chemistry committee and that I am an explicit supporter of the B039 plus B062 configuration; I rely on the specialists on subfields far from my own.
